title: TensoRF scene x component Mirror factorization (synthetic mechanism screen)
hypothesis: When multiple fields share separable spatial atoms, a scene coordinate over shared tensor components will reconstruct unseen fields from partial coordinate samples using fewer serialized bytes than independent dense fields.
physical_object: Three shared spatial factor tables X, Y, Z over a rank-4 scene x X x Y x Z CP field
logical_multiplicity: One rank-4 sampled scalar field per scene
controls: Independent dense field payload per scene
Scene-mode CP factorization (native algebraic control; same 4-way CP function class)
PCA over flattened development fields with fresh-scene code fit from the same observed coordinates

development.purpose: Check fit convergence and code fitting; no fresh scenes accessed.
development.selection_metric: Both development seeds must reach held-out grid nRMSE <= 0.001 after fixed 1000 CP updates; hyperparameters remain unchanged.

task.quality_metric: held-out normalized RMSE and field PSNR proxy (peak-to-peak range fixed to 1)

storage.format: NPZ containing every inference factor/code/metadata array

success_gate: Scoped mechanism signal only if Mirror achieves fresh held-out RMSE <= 0.02 and uses <= 50% of independent dense payload bytes; do not claim Mirror specificity if native scene-mode CP or PCA matches quality/bytes within 1%.
failure_gate: Scoped FAIL for the Mirror-specific claim if quality gate fails, payload gate fails, or the native scene-mode CP control exactly aliases the Mirror parameterization at equal bytes and compute.
boundaries: Synthetic scalar fields only; no images, volumetric rendering, real TensoRF optimization, novel-view PSNR, or FPS claim.
This screen can falsify Mirror-specific attribution for scene x CP component codes but cannot rule out TensoRF Views on real scenes.
Capacity claims require converged fixed-byte frontiers and are outside this screen.
